teaser.text: Citi is a global bank that helps institutions move, invest and borrow money while serving wealthy clients and American consumers. Its dollar comes in through fees, interest and trading spreads, then goes out through funding costs, rewards, employees, technology, credit losses and taxes.

stock.title: Citi stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Citi's stock forecast covers scenario prices, recovery drivers, bank capital and today's valuation.
stock.opening: Citi's weighted price is $127.77 in October 2027, rising to $164.73 in October 2029. Citi's outcome hinges on durable fee growth, falling comparable costs and better RoTCE validating its recovery.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Citi's business works, how Citi compares with rivals, how Citi's management is executing, and what risks Citi faces.

blocks.heading: Where could Citi's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast sees limited one-year upside but stronger potential if Citi delivers its recovery plan. The probability-weighted price is $127.77 in October 2027, representing a 5% total return with dividends. It rises to $144.28 in October 2028, a 20% return, and $164.73 in October 2029, a 39% return.
The three-year outcome spans $116.26 in the bear case to $222.19 in the bull case, against today’s $124.53. The probabilities are 28% bear, 52% base and 20% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Citi?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls to $186.85 billion before recovering modestly, because weaker activity, control costs and additional credit losses overwhelm retained earnings. The bull case reaches $225.85 billion as Services, Wealth and transformation savings lift earnings. Citi targets RoTCE of roughly 11%–13% for 2027–2028 and 14%–15% over the medium term, which supports the base and bull earnings paths but does not guarantee them.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Citi really make and give back?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow works poorly for a bank because deposits and loans are part of the product. A deposit brings in cash but creates an obligation to repay. A loan uses cash but creates an earning asset. Neither movement alone proves that money is available for distribution.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Citi today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings, tells investors how much they pay for each dollar of profit per share. Citi’s trailing P/E is 12.1x, while its forward P/E is 9.7x. If the share price stays unchanged, that gap implies expected earnings per share will rise by roughly 25%.

dividend.title: Citi dividend: payment, coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Citi pays a regular dividend, but coverage depends on earnings, retained capital and bank capital requirements rather than free cash flow alone.
dividend.opening: Citi's current quarterly dividend is $0.67 per share, and the forecast starts at $2.68 per share. The latest year paid out more than it earned; for a bank, free cash flow is not a clean coverage measure, so earnings replenishing capital matter.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Citi's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Citi pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The dividend starts at $2.68 per share, reflecting the current quarterly rate of $0.67. The base case reaches $2.88 in October 2028 and $3.12 in October 2029. That is measured growth below the recent 12% increase, consistent with Citi’s stated aim to maintain payout and yield. The bear case falls to $2.17 as capital pressure forces two reductions. The bull case reaches $3.36 as earnings and capital generation support repeated 12% increases. Analysts forecast EPS of $13.16 for 2027 and $15.00 for 2028, leaving room for the base dividend path.

blocks.heading: Is Citi's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow works poorly for a bank because deposits and loans are part of the product. A deposit brings in cash but creates an obligation to repay. A loan uses cash but creates an earning asset. Neither movement alone proves that money is available for distribution.

The pace of shareholder returns changed sharply. Dividends were relatively steady, while buybacks became the adjustable payment. The latest year paid out more than it earned, even though the five-year bridge still shows capital retained. Repurchases reduced the number of claims on future profits, but they also reduced capital and could destroy value if Citi paid too much.

paragraphs.text: The view would move toward the bear case during 2027–2029 if control costs rise, savings slip, trading and card revenue weaken, or credit provisions increase. A constrained capital position would be especially damaging from 2028 onward because it would slow buybacks and compress the multiple.

earnings.title: Citi earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Citi's next results are expected on January 14, 2027; guidance points to higher returns, while costs and repeatable revenue remain the test.
earnings.opening: Citi's next results are expected on January 14, 2027. Watch whether Citi's growth is becoming efficient, repeatable revenue.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Citi makes money, compares with rivals, is run, and faces its risks.

blocks.heading: What has Citi guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Citi’s central promise is to earn more from each dollar of usable shareholder capital. Its main measure, return on tangible common equity (RoTCE), compares profit for common shareholders with their equity after excluding goodwill and other intangible assets. On October 13, management raised its 2026 outlook to above 11.0%, while reaffirming 11.0%–13.0% for 2027–2028 and 14.0%–15.0% for 2029–2031, excluding a notable item.

The near-term earnings bridge depends on revenue growing faster than costs. Net interest income (NII) is interest earned on loans and investments after funding costs; Citi expects NII excluding Markets to grow in the mid-to-high 6% range in 2026. Non-interest revenue (NIR), including fees and trading revenue, should also grow outside Markets. The efficiency ratio measures expenses against revenue, and Citi expects it below 60.0%.

blocks.heading: Has Citi kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Citi’s 2025 RoTCE was 7.7%, or 8.8% excluding two notable items. The median for large bank peers was 16.2%. Management later reported 12.6% year-to-date RoTCE in 2026 and expected to exceed its reduced full-year target. That is real progress, but the final test is whether returns and controls remain strong after the awards vest.

blocks.heading: How have Citi's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The quarter was weaker than Q2 2026. Revenue, net income and EPS declined, margin narrowed and efficiency worsened. Provisions rose even as net charge-offs fell, showing that Citi was also changing its view of future losses. CET1 remained stable.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Citi's next results?

paragraphs.text: The next report must show whether Citi’s growth is becoming efficient, repeatable revenue. The efficiency ratio measures operating expense against net revenue, so a lower ratio can reflect either genuine cost control or temporarily strong revenue. In the third quarter, reported expenses fell 2%, but rose 3% after excluding the prior-year Banamex goodwill impairment. The below-60.0% target therefore needs to be tested against recurring expenses and continuing control investment.
